name: abbreviation_not_specially_handled
input: Dr. Smith arrived. He was late.
why: Intl.Segmenter has no abbreviation dictionary of its own, so 'Dr.' ends its own segment; downstream code must not assume every segment is a full sentence.

name: quoted_dialogue
why: a closing quote after terminal punctuation stays attached to its sentence.

name: extra_whitespace_between_sentences
input: One sentence.  Another sentence with extra space before it.

expect.text: Another sentence with extra space before it.

why: the double space between sentences is skipped by the leading-whitespace trim, so the second segment's start offset lands on its first real character, not the space.

name: newline_separated_lines
input:
First line.
Second line.
Third line.
why: newlines between otherwise-terminated sentences are trimmed the same way spaces are.

name: unpunctuated_text_is_one_giant_segment
input: No terminal punctuation at all just words going on and on and on

expect.text: No terminal punctuation at all just words going on and on and on

why: with no sentence-ending punctuation and no paragraph break, Intl.Segmenter finds no boundary at all and returns the whole input as one Segment; split.ts is what breaks this down further for TTS. spec/eval/corpus/020.txt (role 'unpunctuated', same idea but with paragraph breaks) is covered by a dedicated real-file integration test in core.test.ts, since Intl.Segmenter still breaks on blank lines between paragraphs even with zero in-paragraph punctuation.

name: four_short_sentences_mixed_terminators
input: Bats eat insects. They fly at night! Do they see well? Yes.
why: '.', '!' and '?' are all recognized sentence terminators.

name: leading_and_trailing_whitespace_on_whole_input
input: Leading and trailing whitespace around the whole thing.

expect.text: Leading and trailing whitespace around the whole thing.

why: offsets are into the ORIGINAL input; the two leading spaces shift start to 2 rather than being stripped before segmenting (which would have desynced offsets from the caller's original string).

name: single_short_sentence
why: the trivial one-segment case: text unchanged, offsets span the whole input.
